text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 paging — elevated streaming tail latency detected for /v1/stream/generate in us-west-2. p95 spiked to 1.2s, p99 to 7.8s across endpoint pool A. Auto-escalating to oncall.

Emily (oncall): seeing the alert. confirming impact — which customers? any error rate?

Tom (support): I have 3 desktop tickets reporting slow streaming responses (customers: AcmeCorp, Litero). No full errors, just long pauses with eventual completion.

Raj (eng-sre): metrics: socket write latency distribution shows a cluster of long tailers after 12:02:00 UTC. No significant 5xx spike. Throughput stable. Snapshot from grafana: p50=80ms, p95=1.2s, p99=7.8s.

Carla (runtime): stack traces show some workers hitting client backpressure - proxy upstream buffer 95th percentile full. Looks like chunk flush delayed by client read window.

Emily (oncall): steps: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) triage root cause 3) handoff if needed.

Priya (prod): customers complaining about UX freeze — please update support and set expected ETA.

Raj (eng-sre): quick mitigation: increase proxy keepalive and reduce max buffering. Flipping these knobs now on us-west-2 proxy tier. Will post commands.

Raj (eng-sre): runbook command I used:

```
# scale proxy pool and reduce chunk aggregation window
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/proxy-usw2 --replicas=12
curl -X POST https://ops-api/internal/proxy-config -d '{"chunk_aggregate_ms":50, "write_buffer_limit":65536}'
```

Tom (support): flipping now. Notifying affected customers: sending templated update.

Emily (oncall): deploying change to proxy config. Rolling restart 3 at a time. Monitoring p99.

(ops-bot): change applied: proxy-config updated in us-west-2 (chunk_aggregate_ms=50). Rolling restarts started.

Carla (runtime): adding verbose logging for streaming flush events on a subset of nodes (10%). Will collect KV-cache/flush timings.

Raj (eng-sre): early signals: p95 dropped to 320ms within 60s of first restart, p99 down to 1.4s. Still seeing isolated 10s tails on a tiny subset (0.02%).

Emily (oncall): any signs of client disconnects or slow consumer patterns?

Carla (runtime): yes — tcpdump sample shows clients holding read window but not ACKing promptly, looks like mobile clients on flaky networks. Combined with proxy aggregation we saw bigger queuing.

Priya (prod): this sounds like client backpressure + proxy aggregation. What's the long-term fix?

Raj (eng-sre): medium-term: add adaptive chunking — drop aggregation for streams with long socket RTTs; immediate: tighten per-socket write timeouts to surface stalls earlier and avoid head-of-line for other clients.

Emily (oncall): implement tightening now: set per-socket write-timeout to 6s and reduce aggregation for unknown clients.

Raj (eng-sre): applied per-socket write-timeout=6s on proxy tier. Monitoring.

(ops-bot): write-timeout change applied.

Tom (support): sent update to impacted customers: estimated full resolution in 30m; mentioned mitigation steps and temporary rate-limiting hints.

Carla (runtime): logs show one customer connection that had constant tiny-ACKs every 12s; we temporarily blackholed that connection for 60s during restart and saw queue free up.

Emily (oncall): current status?

Raj (eng-sre): p95=240ms, p99=680ms, error rate unchanged. Still monitoring for residual tails. Rolling restart completed at 12:11:00 UTC.

Priya (prod): good — please prepare a brief incident summary for customers: what happened, who was affected, and what we changed.

Carla (runtime): collecting detailed flush traces for postmortem. Will attach examples of socket-level timings and a suspect client IP list.

Emily (oncall): handoff plan: I'll run final checks for 15m. If stable, de-escalate and create an incident ticket with severity SC-2 and action items: adaptive chunking, per-socket telemetry, and documentation for support on how to advise customers with flaky networks.

Tom (support): will send final customer note after de-escalation.

Emily (oncall): de-escalating to monitoring-only at 12:23:07 UTC. Leaving this thread open for postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:

(incident-bot): Incident closed to page at 12:23:07 UTC. TL;DR: transient client backpressure + proxy aggregation caused streaming tail spikes; mitigated by reducing chunk aggregation, tightening write-timeouts, and rolling proxy restarts.

Carla (runtime): attaching logs to incident ticket: trace ids [trace-7f3c1, trace-7f3c2, trace-7f3c9] and example tcpdump snippet:

```
12:02:13.123 IP 10.10.2.45.443 > 192.0.2.100.53244: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12389, ack 9876, win 4096
... client not ACKing window increase for 8s ...
```

Emily (oncall): thanks team. creating the incident ticket now with action items and owners.

Priya (prod): prioritizing adaptive chunking in next sprint.

(ops-bot): incident ticket INC-2026-314 created by emily.

Emily (oncall): end of thread.
